editorial.title: Toward provably sound systems that mirror human deductive integrity.
editorial.body: The Vance Cognitive Systems Laboratory at Stanford bridges pure mathematical logic and modern statistical learning. Our inquiry is grounded in the conviction that mission-critical computation cannot rely on black-box heuristics alone. By unifying formal proofs with high-capacity neural representations, we construct autonomous architectures that offer provable bounds on robustness, veracity, and human alignment.

thrustsSection.title: Core Research Thrusts
thrustsSection.description: Each thrust operates as a dedicated theoretical cluster supporting doctoral fellows, published monographs, and peer-reviewed artifacts.

thrusts.title: Verifiable & Interpretable AI
thrusts.description: Establishing rigorous mathematical guarantees for deep representations. We construct automated SMT-solver pipelines that verify neural networks against perturbation bounds, out-of-distribution hallucinations, and safety invariance specifications.

thrusts.title: Neuro-Symbolic Cognitive Architectures
thrusts.description: Synthesizing differentiable learning mechanisms with explicit symbolic knowledge graphs and automated theorem proving. We formulate hybrid engines capable of multi-step deductive reasoning, mathematical discovery, and self-correcting logic.
thrusts.grants: Office of Naval Research (ONR) N00014-22-1-2311 • Sloan Research Fellowship

thrusts.title: Sociotechnical Fairness & Governance
thrusts.description: Conducting empirical post-market audits on large models deployed across healthcare diagnostics, judicial risk instruments, and public allocation frameworks. Formulating reproducible auditing criteria and mathematical definitions of structural fairness.
thrusts.grants: Stanford HAI Policy Seed Grant • MacArthur Ethics & Tech Initiative

compute.title: The Helios AI-HPC Array
compute.description: Dedicated dedicated compute allocation housing 48 NVIDIA H100 SXM5 GPUs tied together via Quantum-2 InfiniBand interconnects. Custom-configured for dense SMT solving algorithms, billion-parameter language-logic co-training, and verifiable weight extraction.

joinSection.title: Join the Vance Laboratory
joinSection.description: We seek scholars with exceptional theoretical foundations, strong algorithmic instincts, and an eagerness to question established heuristics.

roles.title: Prospective Ph.D. Students
roles.description: Admissions are conducted solely via the Stanford Computer Science Ph.D. program. Please mention Prof. Vance in your statement of purpose and select Systems / AI as your primary fields.

roles.title: Postdoctoral Candidates
roles.description: We review postdoc applications on a rolling basis. Candidates must possess demonstrated publication records at top-tier venues (NeurIPS, ICML, POPL, CAV, or FAccT).

roles.title: Stanford Undergrads / MS
roles.description: Undergraduates and MS candidates seeking CURIS or research credits should have completed CS221 or CS229, plus formal proofs coursework (CS103/CS154).
